data.title: JPMorgan Chief Economist: 2026 Could Mark the Peak of the AI Spending Boom
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, JPMorgan chief economist Michael Feroli said history may record 2026 as the peak of the artificial intelligence spending boom, at least in terms of its contribution to aggregate demand. He expects growth in spending on AI infrastructure to slow modestly in 2027, but said investors should not assume the slowdown will hurt the economy or markets. AI-related spending is expected to ease moderately, with gains elsewhere partly offsetting the effect; he also said lower retail gasoline prices could soon benefit consumers as energy markets navigate obstacles from stalled Middle East peace talks.

Feroli said U.S. labor markets had remained relatively strong during the AI boom. While there is little evidence that AI has caused widespread layoffs, he said the perception that AI is destroying jobs could weaken workers’ position in salary negotiations and allow companies to capture more profits. He described AI as a defining feature of the U.S. economy, citing infrastructure investment, spillovers into asset markets, and productivity and labor-market effects, and said reliance on a single growth engine could heighten concerns about its performance.

New York University finance professor Aswath Damodaran said in August that the peak may already have occurred and predicted further pain for AI-related stocks. Apollo Global chief economist Torsten Slok wrote on Thursday that AI had overshadowed other economic drivers and contributed 65% of GDP growth so far this year. He said forecasts for 2027 stock and credit markets implicitly depend on assumptions about the pace and scale of data-center construction. Feroli said any decline in AI-related spending in 2027 could be offset by growth in other areas. The article also said recent market volatility had intensified amid concerns about the AI industry and returns on investment, as well as a scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his subsequent resignation.

data.title: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross to Leave His Post
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Axios, White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross will leave his post, with a White House official confirming his departure on November 19. Cairncross leads the Office of the National Cyber Director, which coordinates the federal government’s cybersecurity policy and strategy.

Cairncross does not plan to serve another two years and chose to leave now so the White House can secure Senate confirmation for a successor before Democrats take control of Congress next January. His departure was described as amicable. The position requires Senate confirmation.

data.title: Maple's Third-Quarter Report Shows $4.73 Billion in AUM and $1.57 Million in Revenue
data.description: GLC Research published its third-quarter 2026 report on on-chain credit protocol Maple. According to Foresight News, Maple’s assets under management reached $4.73 billion at quarter-end, up 2.5% from the previous quarter, while September revenue was $1.57 million, marking a fourth consecutive monthly increase. syrupUSDG reached $375 million in scale in its first quarter, and Maple Institutional’s TVL rose 15.5% to $870 million.

data.title: GTA VI Launch Drives $1.84 Billion in Sales and Creator Content Boom
data.description: According to CNBC, Grand Theft Auto VI sold about 19.1 million copies, including preorders, by Thursday morning, generating roughly $1.84 billion in sales, according to Sensor Tower. The launch also fueled a surge in viewing: audiences watched 125.5 million hours of GTA VI content across platforms including Twitch, YouTube and Kick in its first 24 hours. Take-Two Interactive, which owns the game’s studio, has not disclosed the title’s profit.

data.title: Frontline: Supply Disruptions to Have Lasting Impact on Crude Buying as Asian Buyers Diversify Supply and Hold Larger Inventories
data.description: According to Jin10, tanker shipping company Frontline said current supply disruptions will have a lasting impact on how crude oil is purchased, while Asian buyers will maintain diversified supply bases and hold larger inventories.

data.title: South Korea Exempts Regional AI Data Centers of Up to 50 MW From Grid Impact Reviews
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, South Korea will exempt AI data centers outside the capital region with contracted power capacity of 50 megawatts or less from grid impact reviews under a draft enforcement decree for the AI Data Center Special Act. The law is set to take effect on March 10 next year. The government initially considered a 100-megawatt exemption threshold but dropped the proposal; assessments indicated that many large projects would need a threshold in the gigawatt range to qualify.

Data centers in designated AI data center zones, regardless of size, will be exempt from nontechnical review items and will still undergo technical assessment. Projects designated as major initiatives or applying for bundled permits under the law will receive priority reviews regardless of size. The Climate, Energy and Environment Ministry plans to set out priority-review rules in a guidance manual.

The draft defines an AI data center as a facility equipped with a qualifying scale of GPUs, NPUs or similar equipment, supporting power and cooling systems, and a design power ratio no higher than 1.5. To qualify, a facility must either have at least 250 kilowatts of AI equipment capacity, accounting for at least 50% of total IT equipment power use, or have at least 5 megawatts of AI equipment capacity. The design power ratio is total facility electricity consumption divided by IT equipment electricity consumption. Colocation facilities serving third parties are also covered.

Applicants must report a planned construction start date no later than one year after submitting materials. The government will loosen parking requirements by 20%, with local governments able to raise the reduction to as much as 50%. Server-room and cooling-room areas may be excluded when calculating landscaping requirements; the deduction is 100% outside the capital region and 50% within it. Eligible infrastructure support in designated zones will expand to include transport, heating, energy storage, high-speed communications and facilities supporting local development.

Second Vice Minister of Science and ICT Ryu Je-myeong said the ministries had developed targeted changes to help projects proceed on schedule. Second Vice Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment Lee Ho-hyeon said rule revisions and guidance would be completed quickly while maintaining grid stability. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT Bae Kyung-hoon said the regulations would clarify which facilities qualify for support and the benefits available.

data.title: Michael Saylor: STRC Expected to Draw $5B-$7.5B in Organic Demand at 12% Yield; Strategy Repurchased About $3B
data.description: According to Odaily, Strategy founder Michael Saylor said STRC is expected to attract $5 billion to $7.5 billion in organic demand at a 12% dividend yield, and Strategy has repurchased about $3 billion.

data.title: Bitcoin ETF Holdings Show Mixed Moves Among Crypto-Linked Institutions in Q3
data.description:
Foresight News posted on X (formerly Twitter) that, among the 20 institutions reporting the largest IBIT positions as of September 30, 12 increased their holdings from the second quarter, five reduced them and three made no change. Bank of America increased its position by 740.9%, while Wells Fargo raised its holdings by 103.2%; Wells Fargo’s position had a market value of $2.347 billion at quarter-end, the largest among the institutions listed.

The five institutions that reduced their IBIT holdings were Galaxy Digital, down 49.1%; Avenir Tech, associated with Li Lin, down 30.2%; Marex, down 29.1%; Jane Street, down 18.7%; and Goldman Sachs, down 4.6%. The post noted that these firms have varying ties to crypto markets, but said the IBIT reductions alone do not show that crypto-savvy institutions broadly exited Bitcoin ETFs.

Jane Street increased its Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) position from about 887,000 shares to 7.01 million, a rise of about 690.5%, leaving its overall Bitcoin ETF holdings higher. Goldman Sachs also reduced IBIT slightly while substantially increasing FBTC, resulting in a net increase in its Bitcoin ETF holdings. Galaxy Digital’s other products showed no notable increase, while Avenir Tech reduced its overall Bitcoin ETF exposure despite retaining BITB and adding FBTC. The post said some firms shifted holdings among products, while others lowered their exposure.

data.title: Sherwood Protocol to Wind Down Operations but Remain Open Source
data.description: Sherwood Protocol, described as an agentic financial capital layer on Robinhood, said it will gradually cease operations. According to Foresight News, the team cited growth below expectations and the unsustainable cost of running Guardian Network at its current scale. The protocol will remain open source, but the team will no longer maintain it.

data.title: Tencent Hunyuan Opens Hy4 Model Weights With 1 Million-Token Context
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Tencent Hunyuan’s team has released the weights for Hy4, its flagship native multimodal model. Hy4 uses a mixture-of-experts architecture with 770 billion total parameters, activating 49 billion parameters per token, and supports a context window of 1 million tokens.

The team also published a Hy4 system card that includes a safety assessment report. It plans to hold an online Q&A in Reddit’s r/LocalLLaMA community on Friday from 8:00 AM to 10:00 AM Pacific Time to answer questions about the Hy model series.

data.title: KB Securities Sees DRAM Contract Prices Rising 40% in 2027
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing KB Securities, a report released on November 20 forecasts that the average contract prices of DRAM sold by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix will rise 40% in 2027 from 2026, while NAND flash contract prices will increase 30%. Over the past month, DRAM spot prices fell 5% and NAND spot prices dropped 20%; as of November, spot prices were more than 20% below contract prices.

KB Securities expects global DRAM demand to grow 25% year over year in 2027, against 18% supply growth. Server DRAM demand is forecast to rise 56%, and major customers are expected to receive only about 70% of the DRAM supply they need. Global NAND demand is projected to grow 19%, while enterprise SSD demand is expected to increase 54. Enterprise SSDs account for more than 65% of NAND revenue at both Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

data.title: Kenanga Research: Tech Selloff Spurs Treasury Demand, Yields Have Room to Fall
data.description: According to Jin10, Kenanga Research economists said in a report that the tech selloff had boosted safe-haven demand for U.S. Treasuries. They said markets had fully priced in expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, and that the next key test was whether upcoming U.S. economic data would support bets on further rate hikes in January and April 2027. The economists added that markets were overpricing U.S. inflation risks and that short-term Treasury yields could fall further if economic data cooled.

data.title: BRT.Fit Publishes First Comprehensive Research Report Addressing Project Risks
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Web3 fitness protocol BRT.Fit recently published its first comprehensive research report, a project-initiated self-assessment covering its product architecture, real-world activity verification technology, tokenomics, business model, and long-term prospects. The report discusses risks, unresolved challenges, and unverified assumptions. It states that it is not independent third-party investment research, financial advice, or an investment recommendation.

data.title: STOCKS | Australian Equities Record Biggest Weekly Rout Since 2022 as Miners Slump
data.description: Australian equities suffered their biggest weekly rout in more than four years as mining stocks slumped, Bloomberg reported. The decline tracked a deepening global selloff driven by strains in the artificial intelligence trade.

data.title: Attacker Suspected of Stealing 5.2 Million XMR1 Sells Tokens and Buys 7,467 ETH
data.description: An attacker suspected of stealing 5.2 million XMR1 sold the tokens on Hyperliquid and used the proceeds to buy Ether. According to Foresight News, Lookonchain tracked the activity and reported that the attacker had spent 13.22 million USDC to purchase 7,467 ETH as of the latest update.

data.title: Binance to Add Six Tokens to Monitoring Tag and Remove Seed Tags From MORPHO, HYPE
data.description: According to the announcement from Binance, the exchange will add Lorenzo Protocol (BANK), Initia (INIT), Mitosis (MITO), Harmony (ONE), THENA (THE) and Zilliqa (ZIL) to its Monitoring Tag list on 2026-11-20. Binance will also remove the Seed Tag from Morpho Token (MORPHO) and Hyperliquid (HYPE). The exchange said the changes follow recent reviews and that tags for the tokens will be updated shortly after the announcement is published. Binance said tokens carrying a Monitoring Tag are subject to notably higher volatility and risks than other listed tokens. The exchange reviews these tokens periodically and may determine that they no longer meet its listing criteria, which could result in delisting. Reviews consider factors including a project team’s commitment, development activity, trading volume and liquidity, network and smart contract stability, public communication, responsiveness to due diligence requests, token supply or tokenomics changes, evidence of unethical or fraudulent conduct, and contributions to the crypto ecosystem. Binance stated that other services related to the named tokens will not be affected by the tag changes.

data.title: PowerCompute’s 267 Bitcoin Collateral Sale Repays Nearly $22 Million Loan, Secured Debt Falls to $1.25 Million
data.description: About 267 Bitcoin pledged by Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin miner PowerCompute were sold by lender Arch Lending on September 24, with the proceeds used to repay nearly $22 million in loan principal and reduce secured debt to $1.25 million. According to Odaily, Arch Lending co-founder Himanshu Sahay said PowerCompute directed the sale as part of a corporate strategic adjustment, not in response to a market event. PowerCompute’s 10-Q filing submitted last week showed the company had about $650,000 in cash at the end of September, and substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern remained unresolved. The company plans to raise funds through debt refinancing and a stock offering, which has about $71 million in remaining capacity.

data.title: DayOne Puts Multibillion-Dollar US IPO on Hold as Investors Question Data Center Valuations
data.description: According to Bloomberg, DayOne Data Centers Ltd. has put its multibillion-dollar US initial public offering on hold, people familiar with the matter said. Investors have questioned whether valuations for digital infrastructure supporting the artificial intelligence boom are sustainable.

data.title: CME XRP Futures Reach $81.2 Billion in Notional Volume 18 Months After Launch
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Bitcoin.com, CME Group announced on November 19 that its standard and micro XRP futures had recorded $81.2 billion in notional volume in the 18 months since launch. Through November 16, 2026, the contracts had traded 1.9 million contracts, with average daily notional volume of $216 million and volume equivalent to 42.8 billion XRP.

CME said, citing CoinGlass data, that its XRP futures accounted for about 18.5% of open interest across tracked exchanges at 1:03 AM (UTC+8) on November 20, 2026, ranking first.
